speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens right before and during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and do you have any awareness of what is happening while you are grimacing?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste is a very specific aura that often points to temporal lobe involvement, which raises strong suspicion for epilepsy. Do these episodes tend to happen at specific times of day, such as right after waking up or during sleep, and have you noticed any rhythmic jerking of the limbs or eyes?

speaker: Doctor
text: The post-ictal confusion and automatisms strongly support focal impaired awareness seizures, likely originating from the temporal lobe. To confirm this clinical suspicion and rule out structural causes, I need to see the electrical activity of the brain. REQUEST TEST: EEG
